resources.string:
With a non-original cable, the phone and charger sometimes fail their fast-charge handshake. The phone stays stuck showing the charging bolt while almost no power flows, so the battery still drains. A restart fixes it because it resets the charging chip.

Without root, this app connects to your phone's own Wireless debugging (ADB-level rights, no other app) to command the USB-C port: it limits power, resets the port, or swaps the power role, which can force the charger to handshake again. It measures the current after each try and remembers the one that works on your phone. With root it can also switch the charging input off and on directly.

If nothing works: unplug, restart the phone, then plug in. Also worth trying by hand: with the charger plugged in, turn OTG on and off in Settings (search "OTG"). Long term, use a good cable rated for your OnePlus charger (SUPERVOOC/Warp cables have extra contacts). Cheap cables cause exactly this.

Charge Fix pairs with your phone's own Wireless debugging, once. No PC, no other app.

1. Connect to Wi-Fi (home Wi-Fi is best).
2. Developer options must be on: Settings → About device → Version → tap "Build number" 7 times.
 OnePlus/OPPO: in Developer options also turn ON "Disable permission monitoring".
3. Tap Start below. Developer options opens. Turn on "Wireless debugging" and tap "Always allow on this network" if asked.
4. Tap the words "Wireless debugging" → "Pair device with pairing code". Keep that code on screen.
5. Pull down the notifications, tap "Enter pairing code" on the Charge Fix notification and type the code.

After that it is hands-off: the watchdog fixes fake charging by itself. It works on mobile data too, until the phone restarts; after a restart it re-arms by itself the next time you are on any Wi-Fi. Wireless debugging is only switched on for a few seconds when needed.

Scan phone now: reads the phone's battery records through Charge Fix's own debug connection (no-root mode must be set up).

Bug report: Settings → Developer options → Take bug report → Full report. When it's ready, save the .zip (Share → Files), then open it here. The file is only read, never copied or sent.

Health % = how much a full charge holds today compared with when the battery was new. Below 80% most people notice short battery life; below 70% replacing is clearly worth it.
